caption: A plastic ruler is bent until it cracks, displaying a visible stress fracture that propagates.
scope: Eight predeclared frames, not a full-video or aggregate score
observations: The long central object develops broad wavering, layered ribbon-like edges and inconsistent shape across the sampled frames.
Hands and faces remain more recognizable than the worst R15A example, but the object deformation is not a coherent bending-to-fracture progression.
The physical-process and shape-quality problem is unresolved in this case. Need same-checkpoint no_c and temporal/condition controls before attributing the cause.
With physical fusion disabled, large fragmented patches extend from the central object into the people/clothing; the late-frame geometry is visibly worse than normal.
Normal retains more coherent people and reduces fragmentation, but still produces wavering ribbon-like deformation instead of a convincing propagating ruler fracture.
paired_no_c.interpretation: The branch stabilizes this checkpoint on this example, but does not solve the requested process. Off-branch generation uses jointly-trained native weights, not a separately trained native baseline.
